brief: Generali Asset Management's Fed note covers the FOMC's October 2026 decision. The FOMC held the federal funds rate steady at 3.45%-4% in a 10-2 vote; both dissenters wanted a 25bp hike. Chair Warsh said the Fed has yet to deliver price stability despite some progress, expects Q3 GDP growth to have exceeded 3% annualised, and stopped short of calling credit conditions tight while acknowledging they have tightened for some households and businesses. The Fed also announced it will keep eight meetings a year but devote one to strategy from autumn 2027 and two by 2028, leaving six policy-setting meetings. Generali argues persistent core inflation, solid growth and insufficiently tight credit conditions keep further tightening on the agenda; it forecasts core PCE ending 2026 near 3% and a resilient labour market, and therefore maintains its call for two more hikes, in December 2026 and Q1 2027 (most likely March), expecting disinflation to accelerate in early 2027 and reduce the need for further hikes after that. Market reaction was muted: S&P +0.1%, 2-year yield -5bp.
